## Summary

| Topology | B1 | B1 (alt tie-break) | B2-aws | B2-azure | B2-gcp | B2-best | B1 egress |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `t1_three_tier@core` | 497.58 | 481.18 | 483.57 | 481.18 | 544.29 | 481.18 | 14.44 |
| `t2_pipeline@core` | 1,303.65 | 1,028.79 | 1,033.77 | 1,028.79 | 1,134.87 | 1,028.79 | 274.83 |
| `t3_microservices@core` | 1,822.60 | 1,789.88 | 1,822.60 | 1,789.88 | 2,154.84 | 1,789.88 | 0.00 |

Notes:

1. aws:us-east-1 and azure:eastus have exactly the same price per vCPU-hour for every shape, so B1 has a tie for every component. The reported B1 breaks it by the component's own compute+storage bill, then by smallest location id. This splits T1 and T2 across two providers, and all of B1's egress comes from that split (D-039).
2. No optimum is claimed here. The egress-aware ILP (M10) and the penalty experiment (M15) come next; H1 will be reported against both B1 variants.
